svg.text: Глава 11 · Отказоустойчивые и виртуальные локальные сети
Олифер, 7-е изд. · RAG p0326:c01–p0350:c01 · PDF 326–350 · printed 325–349
1 · STP: make redundancy loop-free
Elect root bridge → lowest bridge ID in source algorithm
Each non-root switch → choose root port with minimum path cost
Each segment → choose designated bridge/port toward root
All other user-data paths are blocked/discarding; BPDU still controls topology
Link failure → rebuild active spanning tree
Classic timer values are source snapshots, not current platform defaults
2 · RSTP: faster state transition
Recognize point-to-point, shared and edge links
Edge port can move directly to forwarding in source model
Listening phase removed; learning/forwarding path shortened
Alternative port backs up root port · backup port backs designated role on shared media
Source reduces failure detection from 10 HELLO intervals to 3
3 · LAG: use parallel links instead of blocking them
Several physical point-to-point links → one logical aggregator port
All members can carry traffic → capacity + redundancy
LAS distributes/collects frames across LAG members
LACP forms/monitors dynamic membership
Upper protocols and STP see the aggregate as a single link
4 · VLAN: logical L2 / broadcast isolation
One physical switched network → several isolated L2 groups
802.1Q tag → EtherType + TCI with priority / CFI / VID in source terminology
Access port → end host / typically untagged
Trunk → inter-switch / multiple tagged VLANs
MAC learning and forwarding are evaluated within VLAN context
5 · VLAN automation and MSTP
VTP → Cisco-specific VLAN database propagation
GVRP/GARP → older IEEE registration model
MVRP/MRP → source-described replacement with less control traffic
MSTP → several RSTP-based trees, VLAN groups mapped to different roots
Goal: retain loop freedom while using more physical resources
6 · Where pure Layer 2 stops scaling
Tree topology leaves some redundant paths unused
Broadcast isolation requires VLAN boundaries
Complex packet-aware filtering is awkward at pure L2
Flat MAC addressing is less flexible for large heterogeneous networks
Inter-VLAN / heterogeneous interconnection motivates Layer 3 routing
Operational reading rule
Redundancy is not one feature: STP blocks paths, LAG bundles paths, VLAN isolates traffic, MSTP assigns different trees.
Troubleshoot in that order before blaming routing: topology → tree roles → aggregate state → VLAN tagging → MSTP mapping.
No vendor CLI is supplied by the chapter.
Chapter 12 starts at p0351:c01 · reading state unchanged · source findings recorded separately.
